hook.text: GitLab has 2,000 employees in 65 countries and zero offices. Its entire company handbook is public and online.

buildup.text: Remote-first companies design all processes for distributed teams. The office isn't the default—async work is.

discovery.text: Remote-first companies save 30-50% on real estate and access global talent pools, not just local ones.

twist.text: Remote work struggles with culture, mentorship, and serendipitous collaboration. Innovation may suffer long-term.

climax.text: Remote-first is a business model choice, not just a perk. It changes hiring, culture, management, and costs.

punchline.text: 2,000 people, 65 countries, zero offices. Remote-first is a model, not a perk.

quiz.question: What does 'remote-first' mean as a business model?
options: Designing all processes for distributed teams with no default office

details.summary: Remote-first companies design their organizations around distributed work as the default rather than an exception. GitLab, Automattic, and Zapier operate with fully distributed teams across dozens of countries, using asynchronous communication and digital-first processes as their operating system.
details.whyItMatters: Remote-first companies access global talent pools, reduce real estate costs by millions, and often report higher productivity and employee satisfaction..
takeaways: Distributed teams operate across time zones using asynchronous communication
Global talent access provides competitive hiring advantages over local companies
Digital-first processes replace in-person meetings with documented decisions

faq.question: What makes remote-first different from remote-friendly?
faq.answer: Remote-friendly companies have offices but allow remote work. Remote-first companies design every process assuming no one is in the same room. Meetings are recorded, decisions are documented, communication defaults to async tools, and no one misses context for not being physically present.

faq.question: What are the biggest challenges remote-first companies face?
faq.answer: Building company culture without shared physical spaces. Maintaining social connection across time zones. Onboarding new employees without in-person guidance. Managing performance without visibility into daily work. Navigating complex international employment law and tax obligations.
